items.title: Jack DeJohnette — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Brought Gary into the band and Nana.

ctx.x: So perhaps talk about how you formed the relationship with MCA.

That was through Ricky Schultz who actually had a label called Zebra Records and this was at a time when independent labels were developing talent that the majors would scout the next talent from the independent labels. So Ricky then got hooked up with MCA, and he was a good fan of mine and we did a deal with MCA. By that time, Rufus Reid had left the band. Mick Goodrick was still in it. Greg Osby, who came to the band, who had a good sense of musicians who would fit in the band. He told me about Gary Thomas.…
…And then “Silver Hollow.” That’s the name of your street.

items.title: Jack DeJohnette interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 7, 2025
items.q: it had Mick Goodrick on guitar, let’s see, Lonnie Plaxico on bass and Greg Osby on alto and Gary Thomas on tenor.

ctx.x: Yeah, a Special Edition album, yeah, the first album I did on oh it was another label, I can’t remember it now, Impulse or — but yeah, it had Mick Goodrick on guitar, let’s see, Lonnie Plaxico on bass and Greg Osby on alto and Gary Thomas on tenor.

I just was looking at the CD Guide to Jazz and they mention both those recordings of yours as whatever critic was writing was very positive about those. A couple of more things before we wrap up, you seem like a patient and thoughtful and calm individual. I wonder if there’s things musically in situations that could aggravate you?
